# ROSACEA

Rosacea is an inflammatory skin condition resulting in erythema and telangiectasia of nose, cheeks, eyelids, and forehead. It typically occurs in mid-life and the etiology is unknown. Erythematous rosacea is the early stage of the disease and usually manifests with flushing reactions and persistently erythematous skin. Late-stage disease is known as papulopustular rosace.

Symptoms include papular, pustular, cysts and nodules. Severe disease results in tissue atrophy and rhinophyma (bulbus nose).

The goal of treatment is control of symptoms, not cure. General treatment measures include avoiding triggers (e.g. spicy food, alcohol), skin care (e.g. moisturizing, gentle cleansing, avoiding topical irritants) and using sun screen. Medical treatment includes topical agents as first line therapy and oral treatment for refractory disease.

## Papulopustular rosacea

Preferred:
Metronidazole 0.75% cream topically q24h ($) DI

Alternative:
Doxycycline 50 mg PO q12h ($) DI for 12 weeks
< OR >
Minocycline 50 mg PO q12h ($) DI for 12 weeks
